sourceOccurrences.label: Mixed-boundary angular operator
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Lemma 2.2 proof, (8)–(9)
sourceOccurrences.note: Closed weighted energy form with a zero trace at 0 and natural reflecting flux at 1 after the angular change of variable. Standard closed-form representation is explicit.

sourceOccurrences.label: Complete Jacobi spectrum
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Lemma 2.2 spectral argument, printed pp.4–5
sourceOccurrences.note: Alternative analytic proof by a ground-state transform and polynomial orthogonality. Complete spectrum -5/48-3n(n+1)/4; both operator-domain boundary conditions checked.

sourceOccurrences.label: Uniform one-arm asymptotic
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Lemma 2.2, (6)–(9) and its final normalization
sourceOccurrences.note: Beta projection gives 18/(5pi). Polynomial sup bounds and the exact spectral gap prove uniform relative error O(exp(-3s/2)), strengthening the fixed-angle asymptotic.

sourceOccurrences.label: Conformal-radius density
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Lemma 2.2, equation (6)
sourceOccurrences.note: Conditional application: radial-SLE identification and conformal invariance are explicit inputs; the analytic asymptotic is proved.

sourceOccurrences.label: Boundary interval density
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Lemma 2.1 and Remark 2, equation (5)
sourceOccurrences.note: Direct consequence of the stated Cardy formula, with the symmetric interval factor, gamma constant and differential identities checked.

sourceOccurrences.label: Stopped boundary conditioning
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, first change-of-measure calculation, printed p.6
sourceOccurrences.note: Normalized martingale, Girsanov drift and convergence of finite-neighbourhood stopped laws under explicit domain-Markov/Cardy inputs. No terminal-law claim.

sourceOccurrences.label: Joint-density operator
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Theorem 3.2, (13) and proof, printed pp.7–8
sourceOccurrences.note: Exact product identity supplies the inverse-square boundary potential. Missing square in the source is recorded provisionally.

sourceOccurrences.label: Conditional and joint conformal weights
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Introduction, covariance display after Theorem 1.1, printed p.2
sourceOccurrences.note: Boundary density factors cancel in the conditional quotient. The printed additional boundary factor belongs to CF; a dilation checks the normalization.

sourceOccurrences.label: Boundary conditioning away from its target
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, conditioning and terminal integrability
sourceOccurrences.note: RSW gluing bounds the boundary connection event below by a local arm; independence then controls every event outside that half-box, without monotonicity of that event.

sourceOccurrences.label: Inverse conformal-radius moment under conditioning
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, final uniform-integrability argument
sourceOccurrences.note: The local comparison transfers the alternating bulk two-arm bound through the conditioning. A tail integral gives every inverse-radius moment below 1/4, including L^(6/5) domination for exponent 5/48.

sourceOccurrences.label: Uniformly bounded strip factor
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, (14), (19) and the uniform-integrability argument
sourceOccurrences.note: An exact harmonic-measure factorization bounds the candidate by 2^(1/3) K4 times the inverse conformal radius to power 5/48.

sourceOccurrences.label: Verification of the strip differential equation
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, (12)–(14) and the candidate following (14)
sourceOccurrences.note: Written reduction to the hypergeometric equation. The stopped Mobius coordinate-change theorem is an explicit input; the calculation uses only the explicit candidate, not assumed smoothness of an unknown density.

sourceOccurrences.label: Three terminal values
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, stopping cases 1–3 and (15)–(19)
sourceOccurrences.note: Under the stated terminal exploration geometry, the strip abscissa tends to zero in every case. Harmonic-measure convergence identifies the limit, and the common integrable bound gives L1 convergence.

sourceOccurrences.label: Conditional five-point density
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Theorem 1.1 and Section 3 terminal representation
sourceOccurrences.note: The density asymptotic follows by dominated convergence under the explicit terminal domain Markov identification; optional stopping identifies the expectation with the candidate. Terminal conditioning and foundational percolation/SLE results remain literature inputs.

sourceOccurrences.label: Alternating bulk two-arm input
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:math/0109120v2, Theorem 4; Section 4, (9), (12)–(16), (22) and Remarks 5–6
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Explicit literature input and scope comparison
sourceOccurrences.note: The continuum upper bound for any exponent below 1/4 is an explicit input to GXMS. It concerns one open and one closed arm; the source exponent proof is not reproduced.

sourceOccurrences.label: Stopped Mobius coordinate-change input
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:math/0505368v1, Definitions 1–2, Theorem 3 and Remark 4
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Explicit literature input and scope comparison
sourceOccurrences.note: AGJ2 uses the theorem with kappa=6 and force weights +2,-2, whose sum is zero. Its collision/target stopping condition is retained.

sourceOccurrences.label: Ordinary-SLE moment scope
sourceOccurrences.locator: Annals of Mathematics 161 (2005), Lemma 6.3, pp.903–904; (6.2)
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Explicit literature input and scope comparison
sourceOccurrences.note: The cited threshold 1/4 is for ordinary chordal SLE6. GXMS supplies a separate conditioned-law argument; no transfer by local absolute continuity or source erratum is asserted.

sourceOccurrences.label: Finite right-force collision
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, two-force driving law before Remark 3 and Lemma 3.1
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Supplementary proof for the stated driving system
sourceOccurrences.note: The maximal SLE6(2,-2) gap system has finite lifetime. A one-dimensional comparison is proved directly by its scale and square martingales; the left gap stays positive and the right gap tends to zero. No trace interpretation is inferred.

sourceOccurrences.label: Integrable endpoint drifts
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, two-force driving law before Remark 3 and Lemma 3.1
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Supplementary proof for the stated driving system
sourceOccurrences.note: A b log b Lyapunov estimate proves integrability of the reciprocal right gap. All three positions have finite continuous endpoints, with the left force point separated by at least the initial outer span.

sourceOccurrences.label: Collision-time tail and moments
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, two-force driving law before Remark 3 and Lemma 3.1
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Supplementary proof for the stated driving system
sourceOccurrences.note: Brownian first-passage domination gives an explicit t^(-1/2) upper tail and finite moments of orders below one half. No assertion about divergence at higher orders.

sourceOccurrences.label: Unique continuous absorbed driving law
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, two-force driving law before Remark 3 and Lemma 3.1
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Supplementary proof for the stated driving system
sourceOccurrences.note: Local uniqueness, compact stopped Girsanov laws and the continuous finite endpoint construct the unique law held constant after collision. Finite-neighbourhood convergence at terminal times and percolation geometry remain separate.

sourceOccurrences.label: Candidate equation with proved target change
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:1011.5822v3, Section 3, explicit candidate and its local-martingale verification before (15)
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Written local equation with coordinate-change premise discharged
sourceOccurrences.note: The needed chordal coordinate change is proved by C6T0/6RZ1/0INI. Together with the normalized hypergeometric calculation retained in AGJ2, this proves the full candidate equation under the stated deterministic and stochastic foundations; terminal percolation inputs remain separate.
